evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文及簡帛字形資料
evidence.text: The database says the graph’s original construction and meaning are unsettled. It records competing proposals: Xu Zhongshu interprets the bone form as a fish and 冓 as two fish meeting, but notes that the form differs from 魚 and remains uncertain; Shirakawa Shizuka sees a tool for weaving cord; Xu Shen interprets it as 一 with an abbreviated 冓, meaning one act yielding two. The database says the oracle-bone context is fragmentary and unclear. It reports bronze examples used for ‘second time/again’ and also ‘two,’ and Warring States forms sometimes add 二 or 口, with 二 possibly contributing meaning. These reports support neither the dossier’s confident ‘two fish caught on a line’ gloss nor a definitive component analysis.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「再」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 《說文》 entry and dated usage discussion
evidence.text: The database quotes Shuowen’s analysis ‘一舉而二也。从一，冓省’ and Duan Yucai’s later gloss that 冓 means 架. It reports bronze inscriptions with 再 meaning ‘second time/again’ (including 陳璋方壺 and 叔尸鐘) and ‘two’ in 𠫑羌鐘 (‘twenty-two’); Warring States bamboo texts include 再三 and the Zuozhuan phrase 一鼓作氣，再而衰，三而竭. It separately reports a possible loan of 再 for 在 in a Guodian slip and marks the interpretation as uncertain. The page does not supply absolute dates for each cited artifact/text, so none are assigned here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「再」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 研訂瀏覽；異體字記錄 A00298-002
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen’s seal-script analysis and records variant forms with citations to historical sources, including an inscription identified as 北海相景君銘 and examples in traditional dictionaries. It establishes that variant graph shapes were documented, but does not give a full dated sequence explaining how the ancient graph developed into the modern standard form.

evidence.field: 康熙字典; 說文解字; 字源字形; semantic entries
evidence.text: The page quotes Shuowen ‘一舉而二也。从冓省’, Duan Yucai’s annotation, and Kangxi glosses such as ‘兩也’, ‘重也，仍也’. It presents graph-form categories including oracle bone, bronze, Chu manuscripts, Shuowen small seal, Qin slips and clerical script; named examples include 前7.1.3 合7660 for an oracle-bone form, early and middle Warring States bronze vessels, Guodian and other Chu slips, Shuihudi Qin slips, Western Han slips and an Eastern Han stele. It lists current dictionary senses including second/again, continued repetition, sequencing (‘after’), degree (‘more’) and supplementation. These modern dictionary categories do not by themselves establish their chronology.
evidence.title: 再 zài — 汉典

evidence.field: Chinese glyph origin and pronunciation sections
evidence.text: This secondary compilation labels the formation uncertain and gives fish-based, rope-tool, and Shuowen-derived explanations as competing proposals. It reports Old Chinese *ʔsɯːs in Zhengzhang’s system and /*[ts]ˤə(ʔ)-s/ in Baxter–Sagart 2014, and Middle Chinese tsojH. These are distinct reconstruction systems and should not be merged. The statement that the ‘second time’ sense developed around Tang is not adopted as established here because the opened character-specific primary/authoritative evidence supports earlier bronze usage of ‘second time/again’.

evidence.source: Wiktionary, citing the Analects and Records of the Grand Historian
evidence.text: The page gives the Analects passage ‘季文子三思而後行。子聞之曰：「再，斯可矣。」’ with ‘再’ understood as ‘twice’; it also gives the Records of the Grand Historian example ‘秦再勝而趙三勝’ (c. 91 BCE) meaning Qin won twice. This supports an old count/iteration use, though the web-accessible evidence here is a secondary compilation rather than an inspected primary-edition page.

gaps: The exact oracle-bone and bronze glyph images and their underlying inscription contexts were not visually inspected; the CUHK and ZDIC pages report cited forms and artifact identifiers. The local Wikimedia seal SVG lead was attempted but inaccessible, so it was not used as glyph evidence.

The graph’s original referent and the relation of its visible parts to 冓, 魚, 二, or 一 remain unresolved among competing proposals. No sound-component claim is supported, so 冓’s pronunciation is reported only as a checked reading, not as evidence of phonetic function.

The earliest attestation of the spoken word 再 and the full chronology of its senses were not established. CUHK reports early bronze uses for ‘second time/again’ and ‘two’, later Warring States examples, and a possible whole-graph loan for 在; these claims are reported separately from graphic origin.

No absolute artifact dates were provided by the inspected character-specific source for each bronze example. The c. 91 BCE Shiji example and Analects wording were encountered only in a secondary compilation; the primary Analects page attempt failed.

The Unicode Unihan records for 再 and 冓 were inaccessible through the web tool. Local Unihan data were available for 再 only (kMandarin zài); no exact local kMandarin row for 冓 was provided. The local Baxter–Sagart rows were checked for both characters, but are repository data, not externally verified source pages.
The accessible sources do not adequately document a complete graphic transition sequence or establish whether any ancient feature was corrupted; no corruption claim is made.
